## panel-search-h
What and where
field service +3 · your state
Change
Search by itself every 12 hours
The desk searches again when the openings are over 12 hours old. Never while the queue is paused.
Learn from what worked
Once enough of your applications have had an answer, openings like the ones that got answers are listed higher. A job's fit number doesn't change.
Remind me to follow up
Days without a reply before an application is marked for a follow-up.
days
Let Claude look for replies in my email
Claude reads replies to your applications through its Gmail connector, and records where each one stands.

## panel-applying-h
Submit for me
Off: the desk stops at every review page, and you press Submit. On: complete applications are submitted without asking.
Practice mode
The desk fills everything in and sends nothing. It makes no accounts and agrees to nothing while this is on. Good for a first try.
Make my accounts
The desk creates your account at each employer with that job system's password, ticking only the site's terms. When a site refuses your password, it resets it through the site's own Forgot password email.
Agree to required notices
The privacy notice, the terms of use and the notice about AI screening that an application can't go on without, and its statement that your information is true. Each one is written in the job's log.
Cookie banners
Declined wherever the site lets you. A banner with no way to decline waits for you, unless you choose to accept those.
Decline
Accept if there is no other way
Jobs at once
How many applications the desk fills at the same time.
1
2
3
4
5
Don't wait for me
A sign-in or an emailed code waits on its card, and the other jobs carry on.
Off: a sign-in or emailed code holds the other jobs until you're done, or 5 minutes pass.
See everything the desk may and may not do
For fixing the desk
Troubleshooting
For getting the desk going at more employers. It searches every list and shows only the openings where the desk doesn't go all the way yet. Nothing is submitted while it is on.

## pw-h
Accounts and passwords
0 of 8 saved
One strong password for each job system. The desk makes them on this computer and keeps them in your computer's password vault, or in a file only you can read where it has none.
If you already have an account at an employer with a different password, the desk can't sign in there until you set this password at the site yourself.
Passwords are shown only when the Job Desk is opened on its own, not inside Claude.

Type my own
Anthropic API key
Optional. For cover letters and for reading your resume, without Claude. Not saved
Save a key
How this works
Each employer has its own account on its job site. The desk keeps one password for each job system, made by the desk or typed by you, and types it only on that job system's own sites. With it, the desk signs you in at each of that job system's employers. Unless Make my accounts is off in Settings, it also creates your account there (agreeing to the site's terms for you), and when a site turns the password down, it resets that account's password to this one through the site's "Forgot password" email. Each password stays on this computer, in its password vault (Windows Credential Manager, the macOS Keychain or your desktop's keyring), or in a file only you can read where it has none. A password the desk makes is used nowhere else. If you type your own, use one you use nowhere else.
An Anthropic API key (make one in the Claude Console, console.anthropic.com, and add some credit under Billing): with Write a cover letter for each job on, Claude writes each letter through Anthropic's API with it (about 10 to 20 cents a letter, written and checked).

## panel-email-h
Your email's app password
A separate password your email provider gives to one program. With it, the desk reads only mail from the job's own site that arrived after the job began waiting, and marks nothing as read. Works with Gmail, Yahoo, iCloud and AOL addresses.
How to make one for Gmail
Not saved
Save
Test it
Test it now
Let Claude read codes through Gmail
Without an app password, Claude reads the code through its Gmail connector while your chat is open, and the desk puts it in.
How this works
Your email: with an app password for the address in your profile (for Gmail, make one at myaccount.google.com/apppasswords; it needs 2-Step Verification), a job waiting on an emailed code or link gets it from your inbox: only mail from that job's site that arrived after it began waiting, read without marking anything read. Without one, with Let Claude read codes through Gmail on and the Gmail connector in Claude, Claude reads it through Gmail while the desk's chat is open (only that job's own mail), and the desk puts it in.

## phone-h
Phone alerts
Off
A push on your phone when a job needs you or is ready for your Submit, and a summary of the day, with this page closed too (while the desk runs). Free, through the ntfy app.
Turn on phone alerts
How this works
The alerts go through ntfy's servers to the topic your phone subscribes to. So they say only counts and kinds ("A job needs you: a bot check", "2 applications are ready for your Submit"), never an employer, a job or anything about you, unless you turn on Say which employer and job. The topic is a long random name kept on this computer, with your passwords; Turn off forgets it (a new one is made next time). One alert a job a stop, those that come together in one; the summary at the time you pick (empty: none). To use your own alert server, open Your own alert server, below.

## how-h
How the desk works
Find jobs searches the career sites of the employers on your lists, and ranks what it finds against your profile.
You pick openings and press Apply. The desk fills each application in the desk's browser window, up to its review page.
When a site needs you (a question, a sign-in, a bot check), the job waits under Needs you on the Home page.
Nothing is submitted until you press Submit, unless you turned on "Submit for me". LinkedIn and Indeed are always submitted by you.
The desk remembers the answers you give, unless you untick "remember". The Your answers page lists them.

## notes-card-h
Notes on the desk's stops
Each time a job stops on something the desk most likely got wrong, it takes a note. Filing the notes is how the next version gets better.
No notes right now.
